# Flow layout rules

The rules a flow has to obey to *look* right, as opposed to the schema, which
decides whether it loads at all. Every one is checked by `pnpm validate --lint`
and shown live in edit mode.

They are measured against the geometry the renderer actually uses — the same
world-space boxes and baked curves it draws — so a finding predicts a visible
problem rather than approximating one.

## Errors

Mistakes rather than judgement calls. Nothing on disk trips these.

| Rule | Requires | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `component-overlap` | No two components may occupy the same cells. | The meshes are drawn on top of one another and one becomes unreadable. |
| `component-out-of-grid` | A component must fit inside `layout.grid`, including its `size`. | The grid floor stops at its bounds; anything past it floats on blank space. |
| `zone-not-in-parent` | A zone with a `parentId` must sit entirely inside that parent. | Nesting is what the parent link means; a child hanging outside contradicts it. |

## Warnings

Worth looking at, not worth blocking on. A hand-tuned layout may trade one away
deliberately — `monopoly.json` is a Monopoly board and has no room for zone
padding — so these never gate a save or fail a build unless you pass `--strict`.

| Rule | Requires | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `pipe-through-component` | No component may sit in the band a pipe sweeps, unless it is one of that pipe's ends. | The renderer drops any component a packet passes over to 30% opacity, so a bystander fades for no reason the viewer can see. |
| `zone-padding` | Leave one cell between a component and the edge of the zone holding it. | Components are extruded boxes seen isometrically: their height projects them up and left, so a flush one visibly overhangs the boundary. |
| `zone-gap` | Leave one empty cell between two zones that are not nested. | Touching borders merge into a single line and the boundary stops reading. |
| `zone-overlap` | Zones should not overlap unless one contains the other. | Partially overlapping fills tint each other and neither region reads cleanly. |
| `component-straddles-zone` | A component belongs fully inside a zone or fully outside it. | Half in reads as a mistake whichever way the viewer takes it. |
| `top-left-occupied` | Keep cols 0–2 of row 0 clear. | The step title and description are drawn over that corner, hiding what is under them. |
| `grid-slack` | The grid should not extend more than three cells past the content. | The surplus is drawn as empty floor and the diagram sits small in the frame. |

## Checking a flow

```bash
pnpm validate --lint             # every flow, findings printed, exit 0
pnpm validate --lint --strict    # findings fail the run too
```

**Tidy layout** in edit mode (or `pnpm validate --tidy <file>`) re-lays a scene
to satisfy these rules: layered left to right, rows banded by zone, then
compacted as far as the rules allow. It is opt-in and one undo, because a
hand-tuned layout will generally come back larger than it went in.

In the app, turn on **Edit layout** and the findings appear as *layout notes* in
the sidebar. They never disable **Save to file**: a flow with bad geometry still
loads, and every drag passes through a bad state on the way to a good one.
